title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
text:
A shepherd boy watched the village sheep on a hillside not far from the houses. The days were long and dull, and one afternoon, to amuse himself, he ran toward the village shouting, "Wolf! Wolf! A wolf is after the sheep!"

The villagers dropped their work and rushed up the hill with sticks and pitchforks. There was no wolf. The boy laughed at their worried faces, and they went back down grumbling. A few days later he did it again, and again the villagers came running, and again they found only the boy laughing.

Then one evening a wolf really did come out of the forest and fell upon the flock. The boy ran toward the village and screamed, "Wolf! Wolf! Please come, it is real this time!" The villagers heard him, but they shook their heads and went on with their work. They were not going to be fooled a third time.

Nobody came. The wolf killed sheep after sheep at its leisure, and in some versions of the tale it also ate the boy.
lesson: Every lie spends trust, and trust is slow to rebuild. Be truthful in small things so that people believe you when it matters.
